papers.title: Usage of Artificial Intelligence in Kolej Vokasional to Teach Construction Technology
papers.abstract: The study explores the application of artificial intelligence (AI) tools within a Malaysian vocational college (Kolej Vokasional) to enhance the teaching of construction technology. It examines how AI integration influences student learning outcomes, particularly focusing on the development of psychomotor competencies required for construction tasks.
papers.methodology: A quasi‑experimental design was employed, wherein AI‑driven instructional modules were introduced to a cohort of construction technology students at Kolej Vokasional. Pre‑ and post‑intervention assessments measured psychomotor skill performance, and qualitative feedback was gathered from participants and instructors to gauge perceived effectiveness.
papers.findings: The incorporation of AI tools resulted in a notable enhancement of students' psychomotor skills related to construction tasks, indicating that AI can effectively support hands‑on skill acquisition in a vocational education setting.
papers.population: Students enrolled in construction technology programs at Kolej Vokasional, a Malaysian vocational college.
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: significant improvement in students' psychomotor skills related to construction tasks

papers.title: AI Competencies and Lifelong Learning for Vocational Teachers: Evidence from Thailand
papers.abstract: The study investigates AI‑related competencies and lifelong‑learning needs of Thai vocational teachers in the Eastern Economic Corridor. Using a convergent parallel mixed‑methods design, qualitative interviews with administrators and document analysis identified key characteristics of AI‑competent educators, while quantitative data from 504 vocational college staff were subjected to exploratory factor analysis to validate a 174‑indicator framework spanning cognitive, psychomotor, and affective domains. An expert‑validated PIERI (Planning, Implementation, Evaluation, Reflection, Improvement) framework was developed to guide professional development. Results confirm three competency domains, seven subcomponents, and high explanatory power, offering an empirically grounded model for upskilling vocational teachers.
papers.methodology: Convergent parallel mixed‑methods design: (1) Qualitative component – semi‑structured interviews with 12 vocational college administrators and document analysis to extract educator characteristics; (2) Quantitative component – survey of 504 vocational college personnel in Thailand’s EEC, analyzed with exploratory factor analysis using principal component analysis and Promax rotation to validate a 174‑indicator competency framework; (3) Post‑hoc expert validation – nine educational experts reviewed and refined the operational PIERI framework across five delivery modalities.
papers.findings: Four qualitative characteristics of AI‑competent vocational educators were identified. Exploratory factor analysis demonstrated strong sampling adequacy (KMO = 0.953, p < .001) and validated three domains (cognitive, psychomotor, affective), seven subcomponents (Computer/AI Fundamentals, Access, Use, Media Production, Communication, Media Management, Evaluation), and 174 indicators, accounting for 82.5% of total variance (domain‑specific variance ≈ 82–83%). Expert validation confirmed the PIERI model as a practical roadmap for professional development across five delivery modalities. The study provides an evidence‑based framework to enhance AI readiness among vocational teachers and support EEC workforce development.
papers.population: 504 vocational college personnel (teachers and staff) from institutions in Thailand's Eastern Economic Corridor, supplemented by qualitative data from 12 vocational college administrators.
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: The psychomotor component is signaled by hands‑on AI tool access, practical use of AI applications, media production tasks, communication of AI‑derived content, media management activities, and competency‑based evaluation processes, all captured within the seven subcomponents of the validated framework.

papers.title: Designing AI-Supported Oral Assessment in TVET
papers.abstract: The paper presents AkoVoice, an offline‑capable, voice‑based assessment platform for technical and vocational education and training (TVET). It replaces text‑heavy assessments with oral interactions that simulate authentic workplace communication, leveraging both cloud‑based and laptop‑hosted large language models (LLMs) while requiring no internet connectivity. A pilot with trades‑training learners showed positive reception and demonstrated a full assessment cycle from evidence capture to teacher reporting.
papers.methodology: A mixed‑methods prototype study was conducted. Researchers deployed AkoVoice on learners' mobile phones and laptops, integrating both cloud‑hosted and locally‑hosted LLMs accessed via web pages. Participants (trades‑training learners) performed voice‑based assessment tasks; the system captured audio, transcribed and analysed it with the LLMs, and generated evidence reports for teachers. Data were collected on usability, learner perceptions, and system performance in offline conditions.
papers.findings: Learners reported that speaking felt natural for the assessment format and that they could better express themselves compared to text‑based tasks. The system successfully completed a full assessment cycle offline, capturing evidence and producing teacher reports without any internet connection. The pilot suggests the tool can be extended beyond trades to other subject areas and education levels.
topics: Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET)
papers.population: Learners enrolled in trades training programs within TVET institutions.
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: The study does not address psychomotor skills; its focus is on verbal/oral assessment rather than physical task performance.

papers.title: The Middle Space in Generative AI and Digital TVET Curriculum Design: A Competence Map Connecting Work, Learning, and Evidence
papers.abstract: The paper examines how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) reshapes both occupational task allocation and the evidentiary standards used to assess competence in technical and vocational education and training (TVET). Using an integrative conceptual synthesis, the authors connect literature on vocational competence, digital competence, digital work, constructive alignment, boundary objects, and evidence‑centered assessment. They propose a competence map that serves as a secondary translation mechanism linking occupational tasks, competence claims, learning outcomes, activities, tool boundaries, and assessment evidence. An illustrative Smart Warehousing and Data Operations prototype demonstrates where deterministic systems remain preferable and where GenAI can add value. The contribution is conceptual: it frames GenAI as a dual disruptor of work and evidence, and outlines conditions under which its curriculum use is pedagogically defensible and administratively proportionate.
papers.methodology: Integrative conceptual synthesis of existing research across multiple domains (vocational competence, digital competence, digital work, constructive alignment, boundary objects, evidence‑centered assessment) combined with a theoretical development of a competence map and a illustrative prototype scenario in smart warehousing.
papers.findings: 1. Responsible digital mediation should be treated as a transversal core capability in TVET curricula. 2. Learners need to make informed decisions about when to use, constrain, or reject GenAI based on task fit, comparative advantage, verification feasibility, and protection of competence evidence. 3. The proposed competence map links occupational tasks, competence claims, learning outcomes, activities, tool boundaries, and assessment evidence without replacing existing standards or rubrics. 4. In the Smart Warehousing prototype, deterministic systems are optimal for structured calculations, while GenAI expands possibilities for hypothesis generation, interpretation of unstructured data, and audience‑sensitive communication. 5. The work reframes GenAI as a dual disruption of work practices and evidence generation, providing a conceptual framework for defensible curriculum integration.
topics: Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET)
papers.population: Technical and vocational education and training learners and educators, particularly those engaged in occupational contexts such as smart warehousing and data operations.
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: Not addressed; the paper focuses on conceptual and cognitive aspects of competence and digital mediation rather than psychomotor skill signals.

papers.title: Fetal dextro-transposition of the great arteries: a narrative review of management and neurodevelopmental outcomes
papers.abstract: The review discusses fetal dextro‑transposition of the great arteries (d‑TGA), a severe cyanotic congenital heart defect, emphasizing that compromised cerebral development begins in utero and leads to long‑term neurodevelopmental impairments. It outlines recent advances in prenatal ultrasonography, artificial‑intelligence‑assisted diagnostics, and multidisciplinary perinatal management that have improved survival, while highlighting persistent challenges such as low prenatal detection rates, limited genetic counseling, unclear perinatal treatment pathways, and delayed neurodevelopmental interventions.
papers.methodology: Narrative literature review synthesizing recent studies on fetal d‑TGA diagnosis, prenatal management, genetic counseling, perinatal treatment strategies, and neurodevelopmental outcomes. The authors searched peer‑reviewed articles, clinical guidelines, and emerging AI‑based diagnostic tools, then integrated findings to provide clinical recommendations.
papers.findings: 1. Prenatal detection of d‑TGA has improved but remains suboptimal. 2. AI‑assisted ultrasound increases diagnostic accuracy. 3. Survival rates have risen due to multidisciplinary perinatal care. 4. Early cerebral hypoxia leads to executive dysfunction and other neurodevelopmental deficits that dominate long‑term outcomes. 5. Current gaps include inadequate genetic counseling frameworks, unclear perinatal treatment algorithms, and delayed neurodevelopmental screening and intervention. 6. Integrated care pathways and early neurodevelopmental support are essential to improve quality of life.
topics: Fetal dextro‑transposition of the great arteries
Genetic counseling in congenital heart disease
Clinical gaps and future research directions
papers.population: Fetuses diagnosed with d‑TGA and the subsequent neonatal, infant, child, and adolescent cohorts affected by the condition.

papers.title: Generative AI for Curriculum and Assessment Design in Competency-Based TVET: An Exploratory Evidence Map with Neutrosophic Annotations
papers.abstract: The paper investigates the current evidence base for the use of generative AI tools, such as ChatGPT, in designing curriculum and assessment instruments within competency‑based TVET programmes in Mexico. An exploratory, non‑registered scoping search of the OpenAlex database was conducted using the FastTrack Convergence Method and qualitatively coded against four propositions. Existing literature shows GAI is frequently employed for assessment and rubric creation, with two empirical studies confirming its use for generating evaluation rubrics. However, no evidence was found on GAI‑authoring curriculum or assessment documents during multi‑year institutional revision cycles, particularly in the Textile Design and Fashion Engineering discipline. The authors propose this gap justifies a future case study in the UTRNG programme and outline what remains unverified.
papers.methodology: Exploratory, non‑registered scoping search of the OpenAlex database using the FastTrack Convergence Method tool; qualitative coding of four predefined propositions with neutrosophic paraconsistent logic used only for philosophical framing; author‑supplied antecedents were individually verified to narrow the search results; no quantitative NPL‑ES synthesis was performed.
papers.findings: A prior systematic review documents GAI use in university course design, especially for assessment and rubric design. Two empirical studies report GAI-generated evaluation rubrics, one in a design/manufacturing engineering course. No documented instances exist of GAI authoring curriculum or assessment documents within a multi‑year, institutional, competency‑based TVET revision cycle, nor specifically within the Textile Design and Fashion Engineering discipline. This evidentiary gap is identified as the target for future exploratory case research.
papers.population: Faculty members at Mexican technological and polytechnic universities involved in multi‑year competency‑based curriculum and assessment redesign, particularly within TVET programmes.
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: Not mentioned in the paper

papers.title: Differentiation between bipolar versus unipolar depression by AI‑based multimodal behavioral analysis
papers.abstract: The study developed an artificial‑intelligence framework that integrates quantitative analyses of facial expressions, eye‑gaze patterns, and voice prosody recorded during clinical interviews to distinguish bipolar disorder from unipolar depression. Using a nationwide Japanese sample of 366 adults diagnosed via the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM‑5, the AI model achieved 78% accuracy (AUC = 0.76) in differentiating the two conditions. Key discriminative features included temporal instability of neutral and sad facial expressions, irregular eye‑gaze, and variability in speech amplitude. The model also predicted symptom severity scores (HDRS, YMRS) based on behavioral cues.
papers.methodology: Adults with bipolar I, bipolar II, major depressive disorder, or persistent depressive disorder were recruited across Japan (August 2022–March 2024). Participants underwent recorded diagnostic interviews using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM‑5‑Research Version. Depressive severity (HDRS) and manic severity (YMRS) were assessed. Video recordings were processed with AI algorithms to extract multimodal behavioral features: facial expression dynamics (including neutral and sad expressions), eye‑gaze trajectories, and acoustic prosodic parameters (root mean square amplitude, pitch, etc.). A machine‑learning classifier was trained and evaluated using four‑fold cross‑validation repeated three times to distinguish bipolar from unipolar depression and to predict HDRS/YMRS scores.
papers.findings: The AI‑based classifier differentiated bipolar from unipolar depression with 78% overall accuracy and an AUC of 0.76. The most important features for bipolar diagnosis were greater temporal instability in neutral facial expression, eye‑gaze irregularities, variability in sad facial expression, and higher RMS amplitude of speech. HDRS scores could be predicted in both groups, with sleep inefficiency, autistic traits, variability in sad facial expression, and comorbid anxiety disorder emerging as strong predictors. YMRS scores were predicted primarily by comorbid anxiety, sleep inefficiency, and variabilities in sad facial expression and eye movement. These results demonstrate that multimodal behavioral indicators combined with AI modeling can provide clinically meaningful discrimination between bipolar and unipolar depression.
papers.population: A nationwide Japanese sample of 366 adults diagnosed with bipolar I (n=120), bipolar II (n=93), major depressive disorder (n=122), or persistent depressive disorder (n=74) who completed recorded clinical interviews.
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: Temporal instability of neutral facial expression, variability of sad facial expression, irregular eye‑gaze patterns, and root mean square amplitude of speech (prosodic variability) were identified as key psychomotor signals used by the AI model to differentiate bipolar from unipolar depression.

papers.title: Mapping discourses of digital technologies: the Mexican secondary TVET system in relation to Chile and Ecuador
papers.abstract: The article investigates how digital technologies and digital abilities are discursively constructed in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) policy documents from Mexico, Chile, and Ecuador. Using post‑foundational discourse analysis, the authors uncover recurring myths—such as a technologically driven new society and a troubled neoliberal past—while showing how each country's political context shapes the articulation of these myths. The Mexican corpus uniquely labels neoliberalism as a past problem and foregrounds AI‑driven futures, whereas Chilean and Ecuadorian texts reproduce neoliberal logics in different ways.
papers.methodology: Post‑foundational discourse analysis applied to three normative policy documents governing Mexico's secondary TVET system, with comparative reference to similar documents from Chile and Ecuador. The analysis maps rationalities, myths, and underlying logics across the three contexts.
papers.findings: 1) Two dominant myths—‘a new society underpinned by digital technologies’ and ‘a troubled neoliberal past’—are present across the three countries. 2) In Chile, neoliberal reforms are implicitly criticised yet reproduced. 3) In Ecuador, education is framed as a right while still instrumentalising digital abilities. 4) In Mexico, neoliberalism is explicitly identified as a problematic past, and the documents project an AI‑driven fourth industrial revolution as inevitable, limiting consideration of alternative pathways. These findings illustrate how myths stabilize meaning while simultaneously revealing persistent neoliberal logics in TVET discourses.
topics: Technical and Vocational Education and Training policy
papers.population: Normative policy documents governing secondary TVET systems in Mexico, Chile, and Ecuador.

papers.title: NURTURE: a Heart–Head–Hands–Feet curriculum framework for sustainable food systems and planetary health education
papers.abstract: The paper introduces the NURTURE framework, a curriculum tool co‑created with an Indigenous artist to embed sustainable food systems and planetary health concepts into nutrition and dietetics education. By organising 35 stakeholder‑identified concepts into four domains—Heart (affective), Head (cognitive), Hands (psychomotor), and Feet (agency)—the framework aims to foster values‑led pedagogy, systems thinking, and practical competencies for future nutrition professionals.
papers.methodology: The authors first compiled 35 curriculum concepts identified by stakeholders from 27 countries. Independent blinded analyses mapped these concepts onto four domains derived from an existing holistic education model (Heart, Head, Hands, Feet). A consensus‑building workshop refined the mappings, after which an Indigenous artist co‑constructed visual representations of the framework on canvas. The process combined qualitative content analysis, expert consensus, and collaborative artistic design.
papers.findings: The resulting NURTURE framework (Nutrition professionals’ Understanding, Reflective values, Translational skills, Utilising systems thinking, Responsible leadership, and Evidence‑based action) positions affective learning (Heart) as the foundation for knowledge (Head), practical competence (Hands), and evidence‑based action (Feet). The model emphasizes diverse knowledge systems, Indigenous values, and systems thinking to equip entry‑level nutrition and dietetics students with the competencies needed to navigate complex food‑system trade‑offs and promote planetary health.
papers.population: Entry‑level nutrition and dietetics professionals (students) and educators; stakeholder input from 27 countries.
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: The framework includes a distinct 'Hands' domain that targets psychomotor competencies (practical skills, translational abilities) for nutrition and dietetics training.

papers.title: Intention to Use Generative AI for Vocational College Administration
papers.abstract: The study examines factors influencing private vocational college administrators' intention to adopt Generative AI (GenAI) for administrative tasks in Thailand. By extending the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) with trust, privacy concern, and institutional policy fit, the authors surveyed 330 administrators and deputy directors. Structural equation modeling revealed that governance‑related factors outweigh traditional technology perceptions in predicting both intention and actual use of GenAI.
papers.methodology: A quantitative, cross‑sectional survey was administered to 330 administrators and deputy directors of private vocational colleges in Thailand. The questionnaire incorporated UTAUT constructs plus Trust, Privacy Concern, and Institutional Policy Fit. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS‑SEM) to test the hypothesized relationships and assess explanatory and predictive power.
papers.findings: Social Influence, Trust, Privacy Concern, and Institutional Policy Fit significantly impacted Behavioral Intention to use GenAI, while Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy, and Facilitating Conditions did not. Behavioral Intention was the strongest predictor of actual Use Behavior, and Facilitating Conditions had a direct effect on Use Behavior. The model explained 82.8% of the variance in Behavioral Intention and 76.1% of the variance in Use Behavior, highlighting the dominant role of governance‑oriented factors in GenAI adoption.
topics: Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS‑SEM)
papers.population: 330 administrators and deputy directors of private vocational colleges in Thailand

papers.title: Never-Skilling in Dental Education: An Emerging Risk of Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: The paper discusses the emerging risk that excessive reliance on artificial intelligence (AI) in dental education may lead to "never-skilling," where learners fail to develop essential clinical reasoning, diagnostic, and psychomotor competencies because AI performs the cognitive work for them. Drawing on the recently proposed concept of never-skilling in medical education, the authors argue that dentistry—particularly areas such as radiographic interpretation and treatment planning—is vulnerable to this phenomenon. They differentiate never-skilling from deskilling and mis‑skilling, highlight potential consequences for dental radiology training, and call for awareness and safeguards to ensure foundational skill formation is preserved.
papers.methodology: Conceptual analysis and narrative review of existing literature on AI in dental education, incorporating the "never‑skilling" framework introduced by Ke et al. (medical education) and applying it to dental training contexts.
papers.findings: The authors identify a previously under‑explored risk: AI‑driven tools may inhibit the development of core dental competencies by providing answers and recommendations before students have independently mastered diagnostic reasoning and psychomotor skills. This risk is especially pronounced in dental radiology, where AI can automatically annotate images, potentially preventing learners from acquiring systematic interpretation strategies and pattern‑recognition abilities. The paper underscores the need for pedagogical strategies that balance AI assistance with active, deliberate practice to avoid never‑skilling.
papers.population: Dental students and trainees (undergraduate and postgraduate)
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: The paper signals that over‑reliance on AI may impede the acquisition of psychomotor competencies essential for dental procedures, highlighting a risk of reduced hands‑on skill development.

papers.title: Competencies and Organizational Commitment of Higher Vocational College Faculty in Xiamen City
papers.abstract: The study investigates how faculty competencies relate to organizational commitment among higher vocational college teachers in Xiamen City. Using a synthetic sample of 360 faculty drawn from a population of 3,602 across ten colleges, the research assesses six competency domains and three types of commitment (affective, continuance, normative). Correlational analysis indicates that overall competency is positively associated with affective and normative commitment, but not with continuance commitment.
papers.methodology: Cross‑sectional survey design with a synthetic dataset. The target population comprised 3,602 faculty members from ten higher vocational colleges in Xiamen. A sample size of approximately 348 was calculated (95% confidence, p=0.50, 5% margin of error, finite‑population correction); a synthetic sample of N=360 was used for demonstration. Faculty competencies were measured across six domains, and organizational commitment was measured through affective, continuance, and normative scales. Pearson correlation coefficients were computed to examine relationships between overall competency and each commitment dimension.
papers.findings: Overall faculty competency shows a moderate positive correlation with affective commitment (r = 0.563, p < 0.001) and a moderate positive correlation with normative commitment (r = 0.488, p < 0.001). The relationship with continuance commitment is weak and non‑significant (r = 0.074, p = 0.160), suggesting competence is more linked to emotional attachment and perceived obligation than to perceived costs of leaving the organization.
papers.population: 3,602 faculty members across ten higher vocational colleges in Xiamen City (synthetic sample used for analysis: N = 360).
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: No psychomotor or TVET signal data were reported in the study.

papers.title: AccreditNet: An Explainable Data-Adaptive AI Framework for Accreditation Quality Analytics and Decision Support in the Training Sector
papers.abstract: The paper introduces AccreditNet, an explainable tabular AI model integrated into a decision‑support framework for accreditation and quality assurance in technical and vocational education and training (TVET). The model combines per‑feature tokenization, multi‑head self‑attention, hierarchical criterion fusion, class‑balanced focal loss, integrated gradients, and performance‑gap scoring. It is evaluated on a structured NAAC benchmark (criterion scores and institutional attributes) using a held‑out split, achieving 93.72% accuracy, 92.84% macro F1‑score, and 0.9706 AUC‑ROC. The study proposes additional operational extensions such as OCR‑based data ingestion, NLP/LLM‑assisted evidence mapping, automated reporting, and deployment in Saudi Arabia, but these were not experimentally tested. The results suggest that explainable AI can effectively support accreditation analytics, pending validation with local data.
papers.methodology: The authors built a tabular AI pipeline that first tokenizes each feature, then applies a multi‑head self‑attention mechanism to capture inter‑feature relationships. Hierarchical criterion fusion aggregates attention outputs to reflect the multi‑level accreditation criteria. Training uses a class‑balanced focal loss to mitigate grade‑class imbalance, and model explanations are generated via integrated gradients. A descriptive performance‑gap scoring module quantifies differences between predicted and actual criterion scores. The model was trained and tested on a NAAC benchmark dataset, with performance measured on a held‑out split using accuracy, macro F1, and AUC‑ROC.
papers.findings: On the held‑out test set, AccreditNet achieved 93.72% accuracy, 92.84% macro F1‑score, and an AUC‑ROC of 0.9706, indicating strong predictive alignment with the NAAC grade derived from criterion scores. The integrated‑gradient explanations provided insight into feature contributions, supporting the model’s explainability. Proposed extensions (OCR ingestion, LLM‑assisted mapping, automated reporting, Saudi deployment) were not evaluated in the current experiments.
topics: Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET)
papers.population: Technical and vocational education and training (TVET) institutions evaluated for accreditation (e.g., institutions represented in the NAAC benchmark).
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: Not applicable / not addressed in the study

papers.title: Preparing students for a global workforce
papers.abstract: The study investigated how artificial intelligence (AI) literacy relates to employability readiness among technical higher‑education students. Using a sequential explanatory mixed‑methods approach, quantitative surveys of 336 students were analyzed with descriptive statistics, Spearman correlation, and multiple regression, while qualitative interviews with 15 students, six faculty members, and six administrators were thematically examined. Results showed high levels of both AI literacy and employability readiness, but AI literacy did not significantly predict workforce preparedness. Readiness was mainly cultivated through internships, project work, teamwork, communication activities, and technical training, with AI enhancing learning efficiency and engagement. The authors recommend integrating AI literacy with experiential learning to bolster professional skill development.
papers.methodology: Sequential explanatory mixed‑methods design. Quantitative phase: validated surveys administered to 336 technical higher‑education students; data analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman’s correlation, and multiple regression. Qualitative phase: semi‑structured interviews with 15 students, six faculty members, and six administrators; data analyzed through thematic analysis.
papers.findings: Students exhibited high AI literacy and employability readiness, yet AI literacy was not significantly associated with employability readiness and did not predict workforce preparedness. Qualitative insights revealed that employability readiness is chiefly developed via internships, project work, teamwork, communication activities, and technical training, while AI supports learning efficiency and engagement. The study suggests that AI literacy contributes to workforce preparation when embedded within experiential learning and broader professional skill development.
papers.population: 336 technical higher‑education students (quantitative survey); a subsample of 15 students plus six faculty members and six administrators (qualitative interviews).
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: Not applicable

papers.title: L’impact de l’IA générative et de la BI sur la motivation professionnelle de la génération Z et les transitions dans le secteur de la construction
papers.abstract: The study explores how Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) and Generative Business Intelligence (Gen BI) can modernize the construction sector and align it with Generation Z’s values and digital fluency. Through qualitative interviews with eleven young construction professionals, the research finds that these technologies improve task efficiency and clarity, boost short‑term enthusiasm and career self‑efficacy, and highlight the need for educational reform and industry collaboration to make construction a more attractive digital career path.
papers.methodology: Qualitative research consisting of semi‑structured interviews with eleven participants representing Generation Z professionals in the construction industry.
papers.findings: 1) Gen AI and Gen BI significantly increase task efficiency and clarity in construction workflows, with AI automating cost and project planning and BI turning complex data into intuitive visualizations. 2) Exposure to these technologies generates short‑term enthusiasm, higher career self‑efficacy, clearer career pathway perceptions, and stronger intentions to stay in or re‑enter the construction sector, especially when accompanied by structured digital upskilling. 3) Successful adoption requires educational reform, industry‑academic collaboration, updated curricula, hands‑on learning experiences, and rebranding of construction as a digital, purpose‑driven field.
papers.population: Eleven Generation Z construction professionals (young workers/trainees) interviewed qualitatively.

papers.title: Generative AI in Clinical Dental Education: Balancing Innovation With Academic Integrity Through Teacher‑Centric Implementation
papers.abstract: The paper reviews how generative artificial intelligence is reshaping dental education, highlighting both opportunities (enhanced diagnostics, simulation) and challenges (academic integrity, assessment validity, and potential deskilling). It underscores the pivotal yet under‑researched role of faculty attitudes and readiness, calls for systematic faculty development, and argues for a fundamental redesign of assessments toward authentic, psychomotor‑rich competencies that AI cannot easily replicate. Australian regulatory guidance is examined as a model for responsible adoption.
papers.methodology: Narrative review of peer‑reviewed literature and policy documents concerning generative AI in dental education, with emphasis on faculty perspectives, assessment redesign, clinical applications, and ethical/regulatory frameworks relevant to the Australian context.
papers.findings: 1) Significant gaps exist in faculty AI knowledge and pedagogical preparedness. 2) Traditional written and knowledge‑based assessments are highly vulnerable to AI assistance, necessitating redesign toward performance‑based, hands‑on evaluations. 3) Clinical integration of AI offers diagnostic and simulation benefits but can lead to over‑reliance and deskilling if not carefully managed. 4) Australian regulatory bodies provide actionable guidance that can inform responsible AI adoption. 5) A phased, teacher‑centric implementation—prioritising faculty development, adjunctive AI use, authentic assessment, and ethical compliance—is essential for successful integration.
papers.population: Dental education faculty and related stakeholders in Australian dental schools.
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: The paper stresses protecting psychomotor skill development by ensuring AI serves as an adjunct rather than a replacement for hands‑on clinical training, thereby preserving TVET‑type manual competencies in dentistry.

papers.title: Gamified Adult Basic Life Support Training for Schoolchildren Using Minecraft Education Edition: Cross-Sectional Program Evaluation
papers.abstract: The study evaluates a fully online, teacher‑facilitated, Minecraft Education Edition program that teaches adult basic life support (BLS) to schoolchildren. Over a 21‑day period, 30 class‑level projects were submitted from 23 teachers and ~850 students across four countries, including Malaysia. Projects were scored with a predefined rubric, and implementation costs were estimated. Findings suggest the gamified platform can achieve broad reach and provide standardized, low‑cost assessment, though it does not measure actual CPR knowledge or skill acquisition.
papers.methodology: Cross‑sectional program evaluation of the 2025 Build & Save: CPR Museum Challenge. Schools self‑selected to participate; teachers guided students through an online adult BLS course and an in‑game building task representing BLS steps. Each class submitted a PDF diary and a Minecraft world file, which were scored by a four‑member jury using a 5‑domain rubric (1‑4 points per domain, total 0‑20). Descriptive statistics, Mann‑Whitney U, Kruskal‑Wallis, Spearman correlations, item‑total reliability, and Cronbach’s α were computed. A cost‑consequence analysis captured provider‑side expenses.
papers.findings: After excluding incomplete submissions, 27 projects were evaluated. The initiative reached 23 teachers and 850 students across Spain, the United States, Colombia, and Malaysia. Median rubric score was 7 (IQR 2‑10; range 0‑20). Internal consistency was high (Cronbach α = 0.95). Projects with an explanatory video scored significantly higher (p = .006, large effect). Secondary‑level classes outperformed primary‑level classes (p = .006). Direct implementation costs were €4,500 (US $5,126); including awards, €6,000 (US $6,835). Cost per student ranged from €5.29 to €7.06. The study did not assess CPR knowledge or psychomotor skill outcomes.

papers.title: Case Report: Neuropsychiatric and cognitive phenomena in a highly complex patient affected by psychiatric and oncological diseases
papers.abstract: The paper reports a case of a 69‑year‑old woman with a prior anxious‑depressive disorder and recurrent endometrial carcinoma who developed a sub‑confusional state, severe psychomotor retardation, akathisia, and tremors after starting combined pembrolizumab‑lenvatinib therapy. Extensive diagnostic work‑up excluded metastatic or primary neuroinflammatory disease and revealed diffuse cortical hypometabolism indicative of a metabolic‑iatrogenic encephalopathy. A multidisciplinary management plan involving immediate suspension of the oncological agents, a structured pharmacological wash‑out, administration of flumazenil to reverse GABAergic excess, and introduction of pramipexole for extrapyramidal symptoms led to complete symptom resolution. The authors emphasize the reversible nature of such neuropsychiatric adverse events and the need for active neuropsychiatric monitoring and close oncologist‑psychiatrist collaboration.
papers.methodology: Single‑patient case report: detailed clinical observation, serial neuroimaging (CT, MRI, FDG‑PET), cerebrospinal fluid analysis, and systematic pharmacological intervention (drug suspension, flumazenil challenge, pramipexole initiation) within a multidisciplinary framework.
papers.findings: The neuropsychiatric syndrome was temporally linked to pembrolizumab‑lenvatinib therapy, demonstrated reversible cortical hypometabolism, and resolved completely after oncologic drug discontinuation combined with targeted psychopharmacological treatment, highlighting the importance of early detection and interdisciplinary management of immune‑checkpoint‑inhibitor‑related encephalopathy.
papers.population: One 69‑year‑old female patient with a history of anxious‑depressive disorder and recurrent endometrial carcinoma.
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: Severe psychomotor retardation, akathisia, and tremors.

papers.title: Regional Heterogeneity in College–Company Collaboration and Generative AI–Enabled Teaching in Vocational Undergraduate Education: Evidence from Multi-Group PLS-SEM
papers.abstract: The study investigates how the intensity of college–company collaboration influences the integration of generative AI (GAI) into teaching processes, and how these AI‑enabled processes affect learning outcomes and ethical risk perception among vocational undergraduate students. Using a structural model tested with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS‑SEM) and Multi‑Group Analysis across three institutions, the authors find strong positive relationships among collaboration, AI teaching processes, and learning outcomes, with learning outcomes also positively linked to ethical risk perception. Notable regional differences in several structural paths are reported.
papers.methodology: A quantitative structural model was constructed comprising College–Company Collaboration Intensity (CCI), AI teaching process (AI_Process), Learning Outcomes, and Ethical Risk Perception (ERP). Data were collected from vocational undergraduate students at three institutions. The model was evaluated using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS‑SEM) to estimate path coefficients, significance, and explanatory power (R²). Multi‑Group Analysis (MGA) examined path differences across the three institutions.
papers.findings: CCI positively influences AI_Process (β = 0.742, p < 0.001). AI_Process strongly predicts Learning Outcomes (β = 0.892, p < 0.001), and Learning Outcomes positively affect ERP (β = 0.635, p < 0.001). The model explains 79.6% of variance in Learning Outcomes (R² = 0.796). Multi‑Group Analysis reveals significant differences among institutions in the CCI→AI_Process and Learning_Outcomes→ERP paths, while the AI_Process→Learning_Outcomes path differs significantly only in one pairwise comparison.
topics: Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS‑SEM)
papers.population: Vocational undergraduate students from three participating institutions

papers.title: Technology-Based Islamic Religious Education Learning Strategies in Improving the Religious Competence of Learners
papers.abstract: The paper analyses instructional strategies that embed the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework into Islamic Religious Education (IRE) to enhance learners' religious competence across cognitive, affective, and psychomotor domains. Using a descriptive‑analytical qualitative approach grounded in library research, the study identifies interactive digital media, adaptive e‑learning platforms, video tutorials, and gamification as effective tools for increasing motivation, material absorption, and devotional skill acquisition. It underscores that teacher pedagogical and digital competencies are critical to preserving the sacredness of IRE while leveraging technology.
papers.methodology: Descriptive‑analytical qualitative study based on library research. The author reviewed existing literature on technology integration, the TPACK framework, and Islamic Religious Education to synthesize instructional strategies and assess their impact on learner competence.
papers.findings: Interactive digital media, adaptive e‑learning platforms, visual video tutorials of worship acts, and educational gamification significantly raise learner motivation, improve knowledge absorption, and enhance the effectiveness of devotional habit formation. Success depends largely on teachers' pedagogical and digital competencies to creatively contextualize Islamic teachings without compromising spiritual integrity.
papers.population: Learners (students) of Islamic Religious Education, particularly the digital‑generation cohort.

papers.title: Awareness and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence Tools among Agricultural Education Lecturers within Universities in Enugu State
papers.abstract: The study surveyed 56 agricultural education lecturers in public universities across Enugu State to assess their awareness and utilization of artificial intelligence (AI) tools, identify challenges to adoption, and propose strategies for improvement. Results showed high awareness of AI applications such as predictive analytics and climate‑forecasting tools, but low actual use of AI chatbots and AI in research supervision. Key barriers included insufficient training and poor internet connectivity, while recommended actions focused on regular AI training workshops and upgrading digital infrastructure. No significant gender differences were found in awareness, utilization, perceived challenges, or suggested strategies.
papers.methodology: Survey research design employing a structured questionnaire administered to the entire population of 56 agricultural education lecturers in Enugu State public universities. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation) and independent‑samples t‑tests at a 0.05 significance level to compare male and female responses.
papers.findings: Lecturers demonstrated high awareness of AI tools (e.g., predictive analytics X̅ = 3.24, climate forecasting X̅ = 3.10) but low utilization in teaching and research (AI chatbots X̅ = 2.10, AI in research supervision X̅ = 2.39). Nine major challenges were identified, notably lack of training (X̅ = 3.36) and poor internet connectivity (X̅ = 3.28). Eleven strategies to improve adoption were proposed, including regular AI training/workshops (X̅ = 3.34) and upgrading digital infrastructure (X̅ = 3.48). T‑test results indicated no significant gender differences across all measured dimensions (p > 0.05).
topics: AI tool utilization in higher education
papers.population: All 56 lecturers teaching agricultural education in public universities in Enugu State, Nigeria.

papers.title: Bridging Vocational and Higher Education Through an Integrated Learning Management System: The eBánki Case
papers.abstract: The paper presents a Hungarian good‑practice case (the eBánki project) that demonstrates how a shared Learning Management System can act as a boundary infrastructure linking vocational and higher education. By integrating curriculum development, prior‑learning recognition (up to 30 ECTS credits) and learning‑outcome alignment within a single digital platform, the study shows that inter‑institutional LMSs can enhance independent learning, improve efficiency, and facilitate smoother student transitions and credit mobility.
papers.methodology: A descriptive case‑study approach was employed, combining quantitative platform usage data with qualitative institutional and pedagogical analyses to examine how the LMS supports curriculum alignment, credit recognition, and learning continuity across vocational and higher‑education institutions.
papers.findings: The eBánki LMS was found to (1) support independent learning and increase learning efficiency, (2) enable measurable curriculum harmonisation and credit mobility, (3) provide a seamless pathway for students transitioning between vocational and higher education, and (4) become embedded in students’ daily learning practices early in its implementation. The authors conclude that LMSs can serve strategically as boundary infrastructures for inter‑institutional collaboration.
papers.population: Students and faculty from participating vocational and higher‑education institutions in Hungary involved in the eBánki project.

papers.title: Beyond Flexible Learning: A Smart HyFlex Ecosystem for Green Workforce Development in Vocational Education
papers.abstract: The study investigates how a smart learning ecosystem and learner engagement mediate the impact of Hybrid Flexible (HyFlex) learning on green skills, occupational health and safety competence, and environmental sustainability awareness among vocational education students. Using a sequential explanatory mixed‑methods design, quantitative data from 172 students were analysed with PLS‑SEM and complemented by qualitative interviews and focus groups. Results show that the smart ecosystem and engagement are strong positive drivers of HyFlex effectiveness and, through them, significantly improve sustainability‑related outcomes, while direct effects of HyFlex alone are modest. Qualitative insights highlight the importance of digital readiness, instructional design, and hands‑on practice.
papers.methodology: Sequential explanatory mixed‑methods design. Quantitative phase: a survey of 172 vocational education students analyzed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS‑SEM) to assess relationships among HyFlex learning, smart learning ecosystem, learning engagement, and sustainability outcomes. Qualitative phase: semi‑structured interviews and focus group discussions interpreted through thematic analysis to elaborate on quantitative findings.
papers.findings: The smart learning ecosystem (β = 0.68, p < 0.001) and learning engagement (β = 0.52, p < 0.001) are significant positive predictors of effective HyFlex learning. Both ecosystem and engagement significantly enhance green skills, OHS competence, and environmental sustainability awareness. Direct effects of HyFlex on these outcomes are smaller, indicating mediation through the ecosystem and engagement. Qualitative data reveal that digital readiness, well‑designed instruction, and hands‑on learning practices are critical for successful HyFlex implementation.
topics: Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS‑SEM)
papers.population: 172 vocational education students

papers.title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence into Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Programme: Perceptions of Educators in Universities of Plateau State
papers.abstract: The study explored how educators in two Plateau State universities in Nigeria perceive the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programmes. Using a descriptive survey, it identified perceived benefits, challenges, and strategies for AI adoption, and examined whether perceptions differed among lecturers, heads of departments, and instructors.
papers.methodology: A descriptive survey design was employed. The target population comprised lecturers and instructors from Technology Education departments of two universities offering TVET programmes in Plateau State. Data were collected via a structured questionnaire and analysed using means, standard deviations, and one‑way ANOVA at a 0.05 significance level.
papers.findings: Respondents identified 13 benefits of AI integration (e.g., personalization of learning experiences, X̅g = 3.14) and 11 challenges (e.g., limited AI awareness among lecturers, X̅g = 3.98). Ten strategies for effective AI adoption were also reported. Statistical analysis revealed no significant differences in mean responses across the groups of lecturers, heads of department, and instructors.
topics: Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET)
papers.population: Lecturers and instructors in Technology Education departments across two universities offering TVET programmes in Plateau State, Nigeria.

papers.title: War trauma and psychomotor developmental disorders in children aged 6–12 in Lubumbashi: a comparative study
papers.abstract: The study examined how exposure to war‑related trauma affects psychomotor development among 300 displaced children (ages 6–12) in Lubumbashi, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Children were grouped by direct, indirect, or no trauma exposure. Psychomotor abilities were measured with the Movement Assessment Battery for Children‑Second Edition, and post‑traumatic symptoms with the French Child Post‑Traumatic Stress Reaction Index. Robust ANOVA and trimmed‑means post‑hoc tests revealed that any trauma exposure markedly reduced psychomotor performance, with no significant difference between direct and indirect exposure. Age, school attendance, and parental support did not predict outcomes. The authors conclude that war trauma, regardless of its form, impairs child psychomotor development, highlighting the need for integrated psychosocial and developmental interventions in conflict zones.
papers.methodology: A comparative cross‑sectional design with three exposure groups (direct, indirect, none). The sample comprised 300 displaced children (mean age 9.55 ± 2.06 years). Trauma exposure was classified using structured interviews, caregiver reports, and DSM‑5‑based contextual assessments. Psychomotor development was assessed via the Movement Assessment Battery for Children–Second Edition (MABC‑2). Post‑traumatic stress symptoms were measured with the French version of the Child Post‑Traumatic Stress Reaction Index (CPTS‑RI). Statistical analyses included robust ANOVA (adjusted for heteroscedasticity) and Yuen’s trimmed‑means post‑hoc tests; regression examined predictors of psychomotor scores, reporting an adjusted R² of .77.
papers.findings: Trauma exposure significantly reduced psychomotor scores (F(2, 111.89)=458.90, p<.001, η²=.93). Both directly and indirectly exposed children performed similarly poorly compared to unexposed peers; no difference was found between direct and indirect groups. Trauma exposure emerged as the strongest predictor of psychomotor outcomes, while age, school attendance, and parental support were not significant predictors. The model explained 77 % of variance in psychomotor performance.
papers.population: 300 displaced children aged 6–12 years living in Lubumbashi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, categorized by level of war‑related trauma exposure (direct, indirect, none).

papers.title: Analysis of Approach Variations in Arabic Language Curriculum Development: A Literature Study on Models and Their Implementation
papers.abstract: The paper conducts a descriptive‑qualitative literature review of 20 primary sources (five journal articles and fifteen books, reports, and seminal curriculum‑theory works) published mainly between 2014 and 2024. Using content and comparative analysis, it identifies five principal approaches to Arabic language curriculum development—competency‑based, system‑based, decentralization‑based, comprehensive, and problem‑centered—and classifies twelve curriculum development models into philosophical and process‑based groups. The study concludes that all approaches and models aim to develop cognitive, affective, and psychomotor domains, offering a theoretical framework and practical guidance for curriculum designers.
papers.methodology: Descriptive‑qualitative library research (literature review) of 20 selected primary sources, employing content analysis and comparative analysis to extract patterns, characteristics, and effectiveness of each curriculum approach and model.
papers.findings: Five main curriculum‑development approaches were identified: competency‑based, system‑based, decentralization‑based, comprehensive, and problem‑centered. Twelve models were classified into two groups: five grounded in educational philosophy and seven in the curriculum‑development process, most originating from Western traditions but adaptable to Arabic language contexts. All approaches and models are oriented toward developing the cognitive, affective, and psychomotor domains of learners.
papers.population: Literature sources (20 primary documents comprising journal articles, books, reports, and canonical curriculum‑theory works); no human participants.
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: The study emphasizes that Arabic language curriculum approaches incorporate psychomotor skill development, suggesting that TVET programs should integrate hands‑on linguistic activities, oral‑communication drills, and contextualized practice to align language learning with technical and vocational competency requirements.

papers.title: Adaptive AI-based mobile simulation for drug calculation competency in nurses: a mixed-methods RCT
papers.abstract: The study evaluated a researcher‑developed artificial‑intelligence mobile application that simulates realistic hospital medication environments and provides adaptive feedback to improve nurses' drug‑calculation knowledge, clinical decision‑making, and self‑efficacy. In a mixed‑methods design, 56 nurses from a non‑governmental hospital were randomized to an intervention (app) or control group. Quantitative outcomes (knowledge test, decision‑making scale, self‑efficacy scale) were measured pre‑ and post‑intervention, while post‑intervention focus groups explored feasibility and acceptability. The intervention group showed statistically significant, large‑effect improvements across all quantitative outcomes, and qualitative analysis yielded six positive themes regarding clinical benefits, realism, confidence, usability, efficiency, and areas for improvement.
papers.methodology: Mixed‑methods embedded design: a two‑arm randomized controlled trial (28 nurses per arm) for quantitative assessment, complemented by focus group discussions with the intervention group analyzed via thematic analysis. The mobile app delivered progressively complex drug‑calculation scenarios with adaptive corrective feedback. Data collection occurred at baseline and after the intervention using a knowledge assessment, a clinical decision‑making scale, and a self‑efficacy scale.
papers.findings: Post‑intervention, nurses using the AI‑based mobile simulation demonstrated significant gains in drug‑calculation knowledge, clinical decision‑making, and self‑efficacy compared with controls, with large effect sizes. Qualitative focus groups identified six themes highlighting perceived clinical benefits, realism of scenarios, increased confidence, ease of use and engagement, training efficiency, and suggestions for improvement.
papers.population: 56 registered nurses employed at a non‑governmental hospital, randomly assigned to intervention (n=28) or control (n=28) groups.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Instructional Practices of Technology Education Teachers in Nigerian Universities
papers.abstract: The study investigated how artificial intelligence (AI) can improve the instructional practices of Technology Education teachers in Nigerian universities. It examined AI's influence on instructional planning, classroom delivery, practical/laboratory/workshop instruction, and assessment/feedback/monitoring of student skill acquisition. Using a survey design, data were collected from 456 teachers (295 lecturers and 161 technologists) across 13 federal universities through questionnaires and semi‑structured interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed with means, standard deviations, and t‑tests; qualitative data were thematically analysed. Results identified 11 ways AI can enhance each instructional area, with mean ratings ranging from 3.30 to 3.72, and showed no significant differences between lecturers and technologists. Qualitative insights supported these findings, highlighting AI's potential to aid lesson preparation, delivery, practical demonstrations, assessment efficiency, and student monitoring.
papers.methodology: Survey research design; population of 456 Technology Education teachers (295 lecturers, 161 technologists) from 13 federal universities in Nigeria; data collection via structured questionnaire and semi‑structured interview guide; quantitative analysis employing mean, standard deviation, and independent‑samples t‑test; qualitative data summarised through thematic analysis.
papers.findings: AI was found to enhance instructional planning (mean = 3.61), classroom instructional delivery (mean = 3.53), practical/laboratory/workshop‑based instruction (mean = 3.30), and assessment, feedback, and monitoring of students’ skill acquisition (mean = 3.72). No statistically significant differences were observed between lecturers and technologists across all instructional practice areas at the 0.05 significance level. Qualitative results corroborated these quantitative outcomes, indicating AI’s role in improving lesson preparation, delivery, practical demonstrations, assessment efficiency, and student monitoring.
papers.population: 456 Technology Education teachers (295 lecturers and 161 technologists) from 13 federal universities in Nigeria.
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: The study highlights AI's potential to enhance practical, laboratory, and workshop‑based instruction, thereby supporting the development of students' psychomotor skills in technology vocational education and training (TVET).

papers.title: Determinant of artificial intelligence skills adoption among built environment professionals in a developing economy
papers.abstract: The paper examines what drives the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) competencies among built‑environment professionals in Nigeria, a developing economy. Using a quantitative survey of construction practitioners, the study identifies four principal determinants of AI skill uptake. The results aim to inform policymakers, professional bodies, and educational institutions on how to boost digital capabilities in the construction sector.
papers.methodology: A quantitative research design was employed. Data were collected through structured questionnaires distributed to construction professionals in Nigeria. Descriptive statistics and inferential techniques were applied, and exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was used to uncover underlying determinants of AI skills adoption.
papers.findings: Four key determinants emerged from the EFA: (1) AI skills awareness and readiness, (2) attitudinal readiness, (3) institutional and policy environment, and (4) resource accessibility factors. These determinants collectively influence the extent to which built‑environment professionals adopt AI competencies.
papers.population: Construction and built‑environment professionals in Nigeria
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: The study does not explicitly address psychomotor TVET signals; it focuses on cognitive and attitudinal factors influencing AI skill adoption.

papers.title: Implementasi Media MESICA dalam Pembelajaran IPA: Studi Kualitatif Terhadap Proses dan Respon Siswa pada Materi Sifat-Sifat Cahaya di Kelas V SD
papers.abstract: The study examined the implementation of the MESICA (Media Sifat Cahaya) instructional medium in fifth‑grade science lessons on the properties of light at an elementary school in East Jakarta. Using a qualitative case‑study design, the researchers observed classroom activities, conducted interviews, and collected documentation to assess how the medium affected teaching processes and student responses. Findings indicated that MESICA facilitated active learning through observation, experimentation, and discussion, leading to improved cognitive understanding, positive affective reactions, and enhanced psychomotor engagement among students.
papers.methodology: Qualitative case‑study approach; purposive sampling of a classroom teacher and selected fifth‑grade students; data collected via classroom observation, semi‑structured interviews, and document analysis; data analyzed with Miles and Huberman’s systematic model (data reduction, data display, conclusion drawing); trustworthiness ensured through source and technique triangulation.
papers.findings: MESICA was integrated into learning activities involving observation, hands‑on experiments, and group discussion, which promoted active student involvement. Students displayed a clearer conceptual grasp of light properties, expressed enthusiasm and interest (affective), and actively participated in experimental procedures, indicating psychomotor development. Overall, MESICA proved to be an effective alternative medium for active and meaningful elementary science instruction.
papers.population: Fifth‑grade (Class V) students at SDN Baru 06 Pagi, East Jakarta, Indonesia, and their classroom teacher (selected via purposive sampling).
papers.psychomotor_tvet_signals: Students engaged in hands‑on experiments, manipulated light‑related equipment, and participated in group activities, demonstrating development of fine‑motor and procedural skills relevant to technical‑vocational contexts.

papers.title: Development of Context-based Learning Activities to Promote the Learning Achievement of Vocational Students
authors: ภูษิต บุญทองเถิง
papers.abstract: The study developed context‑based learning activities for vocational nursing students and examined their impact on academic achievement and learner satisfaction. Using a pre‑test/post‑test design with 30 students from Ganzhou Vocational School of Applied Technique, the authors found that the activities were judged highly suitable by experts, significantly improved post‑test scores compared with pre‑test scores, and generated high overall satisfaction among participants.
papers.methodology: A quasi‑experimental pre‑test/post‑test design was employed. Thirty first‑semester nursing students were selected through whole random sampling. Researchers created lesson plans incorporating context‑based learning activities, administered learning achievement tests before and after the intervention, and collected satisfaction data via questionnaires. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation) and inferential statistics (paired t‑test) to assess changes in achievement and satisfaction levels.
papers.findings: 1) Expert evaluation rated the developed context‑based learning activities as highly suitable (average score 4.29/5). 2) Students’ post‑test academic achievement scores were significantly higher than pre‑test scores (p < .01). 3) Students reported a high level of overall satisfaction with the learning activities.
papers.population: 30 nursing students enrolled in the first semester of 2025 at Ganzhou Vocational School of Applied Technique, selected via whole random sampling.
